editorial.headline: KBLI 46599: Machinery Wholesale, Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This broad machinery-wholesale activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet PMA registration in Bali is blocked under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46599 covers wholesale trade in machinery, equipment and associated supplies that fall outside more specifically grouped machinery activities. Its practical territory is wide: prime movers, turbines and power-generation machines; production robots other than processing robots; trade, navigation and service machinery; cables, switches and installation equipment; machine tools; measuring equipment; and mining, construction and civil-engineering equipment such as excavators. It also includes traffic barriers, bollards, street and traffic lights, road signs, and bus- and tram-stop equipment. The scope extends to wholesale of weapons, weapons systems and ammunition, including tanks and armoured combat vehicles.

That breadth matters because this is not a single-product activity. It is a wholesale classification for businesses supplying industrial, infrastructure, technical and public-realm equipment across a varied set of use cases. The record opens it to operators at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, allowing the activity to serve businesses from micro through large scale. What unifies the category is the wholesale function and the equipment-led nature of the trade, rather than one customer sector or one type of machinery.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear: the activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the entire national ownership allowance for this activity. In Bali, however, the answer changes decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope within the record is assessed by OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah, placing it within Bali’s moratorium.

That is an island-wide, permanent provincial rule: Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The block is recorded under the Bali risk-class status Blocked (risk class) and is tied to the moratorium of 13 May 2026. The distinction is essential for founders: national openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remain real features of the activity, but they do not make PMA registration available in Bali where the provincial risk-based restriction applies.
